rows.text: Sheoldred does both halves of a sacrifice deck at once: she reanimates a creature for free on your upkeep, and she makes every opponent sacrifice one on theirs. So the deck is built out of high-impact creatures that want to die or enter—Archon of Cruelty, Vilis, Razaketh, Kokusho—and outlets to recycle them on your own terms. Early on, cheap reanimation spells cheat monsters into play on turns 1 to 3; later, Sheoldred and Mikaeus take over to lock out or kill the entire table.
Bracket 3: the Game Changer cap is three, filled by Demonic Tutor, Opposition Agent, and The One Ring. No mass land denial. Assemble infinite combo lines from turn 6 onward.

rows.name: Mikaeus, the Unhallowed + Triskelion
rows.text: Triskelion enters with three +1/+1 counters and gains +1/+1 from Mikaeus. Remove one counter to deal 1 damage to an opponent, then remove the other two counters to deal 2 damage to Triskelion itself. With zero counters, Triskelion dies as a 2/2 with two damage marked. Undying triggers and returns Triskelion with an additional +1/+1 counter (now four counters total). Repeat the loop removing two counters to ping opponents and two to kill itself, dealing infinite damage to all opponents.

rows.name: Buried Alive -> Mikaeus, the Unhallowed + Triskelion
rows.text: the primary winning pile. Entomb both pieces alongside a third threat (like Gray Merchant or Archon of Cruelty); return them together with Victimize, Living Death, or Agadeem's Awakening to end the game on the spot.

rows.name: Vilis, Broker of Blood
rows.text: an 8/8 flying demon that draws cards whenever you lose life. Cheating him out with Reanimate loses eight life, immediately drawing eight fresh cards for a single black mana.

rows.name: Razaketh, the Foulblooded
rows.text: an 8/8 flying trample demon that sacrifices any creature for two life to tutor any card to hand at instant speed, effortlessly chaining tutors into your winning combo.

rows.name: Archon of Cruelty

rows.name: Kokusho, the Evening Star
rows.text: drains five life from each opponent and heals you for fifteen whenever it dies. Bringing it back on upkeep and sacrificing it drains the table for fifteen life every turn cycle.

rows.name: Junji, the Midnight Sky
rows.text: forces discards and drains life when it dies, or reanimates another creature from your graveyard.

rows.name: Grave Titan

rows.name: Sephiroth, Fabled SOLDIER

rows.text: redirects opposing targeted removal spells or counterspells.

A playable opening hand requires two or three mana sources, a discard outlet or self-mill enabler (Entomb, Stitcher's Supplier, Buried Alive, Bitter Triumph), and a reanimation spell (Reanimate, Animate Dead, Necromancy, Victimize). Hands with big 8-drops but no way to discard or reanimate them are unplayable.
In the early turns, use Dark Ritual or cheap reanimation to get Archon of Cruelty or Vilis into play on turn 2 or 3 to bury the table in card advantage.

When preparing to win on turn 6 or later, cast Buried Alive to bin Mikaeus, the Unhallowed and Triskelion, then return them with Victimize or Living Death to execute the infinite damage loop. If a combo finish is not available, Sheoldred and Grave Pact will starve the table of creatures while Kokusho and Gray Merchant drain opponents out.
